name: Pulpblow
description: Raise the mace past the ear and drop the knobbed head straight down onto the target's guard or shoulder.

name: Poundbump
description: Swing the mace across the body from the strong side, whipping the head into the ribs with a hip turn.

name: Ready Wristloop
description: Angle the haft against an incoming blow and turn it aside along the wood, away from the body.

name: Backward Pearhead
description: Slide the rear foot forward and re-plant, keeping the head up and the weight over the haft hand.

name: Ironknob Hit
description: Shorten the grip and jab the mace's rounded head straight into the opponent's belly to bend them over.

name: Peardash
description: Rake a flanged edge across the target's forearm in a short sideways swing to loosen its grip.

name: Crush Bump
description: Strike down, let the head rebound off the target, and bring the mace back up along the same line.

name: Haftring Stay
description: Grip the haft at both ends and hold it flat across the chest to stop a descending blow.

name: Quiet Maceball
description: Pivot on the lead heel to turn the body off the line of attack while keeping the mace raised.

name: Short Ribhead
description: Drive the haft's butt cap forward into the opponent's chest as they close the distance.

name: Crushwedge
description: Roll the wrist to spin the head in a small circle, pulling an opponent's reaching hand off balance.

name: Short Studhead
description: Lift the mace slowly overhead and lower it in a controlled arc to build the shoulders for heavy blows.

name: Leaden Flangerib
description: Plant the legs wide and swing the head low, striking the thigh and knee of a standing opponent.

name: Stepping Pulp
description: Advance with the mace resting across the shoulder, shifting weight evenly so the heavy head never drags the stance.

name: Snug Maceneck
description: Sweep the haft diagonally across the body to knock a thrust or swing aside from the ribs.

name: Catching Dent
description: Press the mace's knob onto a gripped limb and lean in to pin it against the opponent's own body.

name: Pound Hit
description: Chain three swings to one breath, striking high, middle and low in a steady rhythm without resetting the grip.

name: Angled Maceneck
description: Let the mace head settle to the ground and brace behind the haft, taking a shove by weight alone.

name: Fouling Flangerib
description: Swing the head halfway down on the lead side to draw a flinch, then redirect to the opposite shoulder.

name: Quiet Pound
description: Step in until the haft's length just reaches the opponent, setting the distance for every following swing.

name: Upward Pearhead
description: Rap the mace head against the outside of an opponent's elbow to numb the arm and spoil its grip.

name: Macelid
description: Lift the mace from low guard to knock an incoming weapon upward and open the opponent's body.

name: Tripping Bellhead
description: Hook the flange behind a shield rim or sleeve and tug it sideways to unbalance the holder.

name: Firm Studhead
description: Bring the head down at a steep angle onto the collarbone, aiming to stagger rather than fell.

name: Sturdy Batter
description: Swing the heavy head in a full overhead arc and drop it onto the target with the whole back behind it.

name: Ribpause
description: Turn the mace so the flange meets the incoming edge and rolls it away from the knuckles.

name: Pearstay
description: Sink into a wide planted stance with the mace across the thighs to ride out a charge.

name: Pearblow
description: Sweep the mace head low through the opponent's knee as they step in, buckling the leg.

name: Dentstay
description: Hook the haft's pommel behind the opponent's wrist and pull to draw the arm across their body.

name: Batterpause
description: Catch an opponent's swinging weapon on the haft just below the head and wrench it aside.

name: Descending Ironknob
description: Check the swing early and knock the head sharply against the opponent's hand to stop their advance.

name: Sudden Haftring
description: Flick the wrist to snap the short haft's head into an exposed hand or forearm.

name: Pulphit
description: Draw the mace from the belt and bring it up into the first blow in one motion.

name: Denthit
description: Close the gap and drive the knob into the ribs where a longer weapon cannot swing.

name: Ribhead Lid
description: Let the mace hang from its wrist loop, catch it back in hand, and swing again after a missed strike.

name: Pulp Hop
description: Slip off the line to the outside and rap the opponent's lead hand in the same step.

name: Pearwedge
description: Lay the short haft along the forearm and take a blow on both together to protect the elbow.

name: Narrow Smash
description: Send a thread of qi into the head as it falls so the blow lands heavier than muscle alone.

name: Planted Bellhead
description: Run qi along the haft and knock aside a blade with a firm, ringing turn of the wood.

name: Gnawing Smash
description: Strike with the flange edge while pushing qi through it, cracking a plate edge or bruising through padding.

name: Backward Batter
description: Draw a breath of qi into the legs and cover two paces behind the mace in one stride.

name: Crushcowl
description: Settle qi in the palms to hold the haft steady while the opponent's weapon grinds against it.

name: Straight Dent
description: Knock the knob into an opponent's guard hand to open the line for a follow-up swing.

name: Quick Crush
description: Aim the flange at mail links and drive qi through them so the shock reaches the flesh beneath.

name: Single Wristloop
description: Thump the head through a padded coat to bruise the ribs without needing a clean edge.

name: Single Pulp
description: Strike the rim of a breastplate where it meets the arm to dent it and jar the wearer.

name: Open Smash
description: Tap the side of a helm with a short sharp swing so the ring of the blow dazes.

name: Macepause
description: Roll the haft around an incoming blade to turn it down and away from the body.

name: Denthusk
description: Hook the flange behind a gauntlet cuff and pin the hand against the opponent's waist.

name: Backward Maceball
description: Shift weight onto the front foot and settle qi low, readying the next heavy swing.

name: Leaden Maceneck
description: Swing the light head in a quick flat arc to strike the opponent's shield rim and shake the arm behind it.

name: Maceball Dash
description: Let the head carry past the target, turn the wrist, and bring it back across the opposite flank.

name: Folded Flangerib
description: Step back and flick the haft up so the blow glances off it instead of the body.

name: Easing Dent
description: Slide sideways while lowering the head, resetting the stance for the next swing.

name: Pulpwedge
description: Poke the knob at a swinging arm's inner side to stop the swing before it builds.

name: Solid Ribhead
description: Raise the mace flat overhead and hold qi through the haft to take a descending blow.

name: Wristloop Cowl
description: Lower the head to the front shin and brace the haft to stop a low cut or kick.

name: Sharp Haftring
description: Beat the incoming weapon aside with the flange and swing the head straight back into the opening.

name: Studhead Hop
description: Dip under a horizontal swing and rise inside, mace already cocked at the shoulder.

name: Batterlid
description: Cross the haft over an opponent's weapon, lock both, and press until their arm tires.

name: Batterdrop
description: Answer a parry by turning the knob into the opponent's wrist as it overreaches.

name: Snug Ironknob
description: Brace the haft across a narrow passage to halt a rush while the mace head threatens the nearest attacker.

name: Pearlid
description: Check an approaching attacker's shoulder with the haft's side to turn them aside in a press of bodies.

name: Wide Crush
description: Rap the head in a short arc against a hand reaching for the escorted person or cargo.

name: Blunt Bellhead
description: Choke up on the haft and strike with the knob where a full swing would hit a bystander.

name: Swaying Flangerib
description: Pivot around a cart or doorpost to keep the mace between the escorted person and the attacker.

name: Straight Pound
description: Jab the haft's butt backward into a pursuer's stomach without turning the head or the feet.

name: Batter Amble
description: Retreat one short step at a time, keeping the head raised and the escorted person at the back.

name: Nabbing Batter
description: Beat the head against an armored post or plate to startle a wary opponent into hesitating.

name: Pearhead Lid
description: Hold the mace still after a block and let the flange catch the opponent's weapon so it cannot slide free.

name: Macehit
description: Keep the wrist locked through a swing and let qi settle in the forearm so the head lands true.

name: Pearcowl
description: Let a hard parry rebound off the haft and catch the head again at once for the next blow.

name: Solid Haftring
description: Exhale as the blow lands and let qi sink through the haft into the planted feet.

name: Forward Pound
description: Rake the flange down the length of an opponent's weapon arm to scrape the hand open.

name: Sideways Crush
description: Advance in half-paces behind the guard, never lifting the mace head above the shoulder line.
